However, the court may make an order under subsection (3) only if, after hearing from the person for whose protection the registered corresponding New Zealand order was made, the court is satisfied that revealing that the person is in Victoria would not jeopardise the safety of the person or any children of the person.
If the court makes an order under subsection (3) the court must arrange for the registered corresponding New Zealand order to be served on the respondent.

nodes.heading: Effect of registration of corresponding New Zealand orders

nodes.text: A corresponding New Zealand order—
has the same effect in Victoria as it has for the time being in New Zealand; and
may be enforced against a person as if it were a final order under this Act.
A contravention of the New Zealand order in Victoria is taken, for the purposes of imposing a penalty, to be a contravention of a final order.

nodes.heading: Variation, revocation or extension of corresponding New Zealand order
nodes.text: If a corresponding New Zealand order registered under this Division is varied, revoked or extended by a court in New Zealand—
the registration is varied, revoked or extended accordingly; and
the appropriate registrar must give the Chief Commissioner of Police notice of the variation, revocation or extension. __________________

nodes.heading: Constitution of court
nodes.text: The court, when exercising a power under this Part, must be constituted by—
for the Magistrates' Court, the Chief Magistrate or a Deputy Chief Magistrate; or
for the Children's Court, the President of the Court.

nodes.heading: Who may apply for order that person is a vexatious litigant

nodes.text: The following persons may apply to the court for an order declaring a person to be a vexatious litigant—
the Attorney-General;
a person against whom applications have been made under this Act or the Crimes (Family Violence) Act 1987;
a person against whom complaints have been made under the Crimes (Family Violence) Act 1987.
However, a person other than the Attorney-General may apply for an order under subsection
only with the leave of a magistrate of the court.
A magistrate may grant leave under subsection (2) for an application if the magistrate is satisfied there is evidence that—
there is merit in the application; and
the making of the application would not be an abuse of process.

nodes.heading: Attorney-General may request documents from courts

nodes.text: For the purposes of deciding whether to make an application under section 189(1) for an order declaring a person to be a vexatious litigant, the Attorney-General may ask a court for a copy of documents held by the court in relation to a proceeding brought under this Act or the Crimes (Family Violence) Act 1987 by the person.
The court may give to the Attorney-General a copy of documents requested under subsection (1).

nodes.heading: Notice of application by Attorney-General to be served on protected person
nodes.text: If the Attorney-General applies under section 189(1) for an order declaring a person to be a vexatious litigant, the appropriate registrar for the court must serve a copy of the application on the person who would be protected by the order.

nodes.heading: Notice of application to be served on person proposed to be declared vexatious litigant
nodes.text: A copy of an application for an order declaring a person to be a vexatious litigant must be served by the appropriate registrar for the court on the person who it is proposed will be declared a vexatious litigant.

nodes.heading: Order declaring person to be vexatious litigant

nodes.text: The court may, after hearing or giving the person an opportunity to be heard, make an order declaring the person to be a vexatious litigant if it is satisfied the person has habitually, persistently and without any reasonable ground instituted proceedings under this Act against the same person.

An order under subsection (1) must provide that the vexatious litigant must not without leave of the court make an application for a family violence intervention order, or the variation, revocation or extension of a family violence intervention order, in relation to a person stated in the order or the person's children.
The appropriate registrar for the court must serve a copy of an order made under subsection (1) on—
the vexatious litigant; and
the person protected by the order; and
the Attorney-General.
The order must include or be accompanied by a statement of the court's reasons for the decision.

nodes.heading: Leave to make an application under this Act

nodes.text: For the purposes of deciding an application by a vexatious litigant for leave to make an application for a family violence intervention order, or the variation, revocation or extension of a family violence intervention order, the court may be constituted by any magistrate.
The application must be decided by the court as soon as practicable.

nodes.heading: Appeal against order declaring person to be vexatious litigant

nodes.text: A person who is declared to be a vexatious litigant by an order made under this Part may appeal against the order to—
the County Court, with the leave of that Court; or
if the court that made the relevant decision was the Children's Court constituted by the President of the Court, the Trial Division of the Supreme Court with the leave of that Court.
The appropriate registrar for the Court must serve notice of the application for leave on—
the person protected by the order; and
if the Attorney-General made the application under section 189(1)(a) for the order declaring the person to be a vexatious litigant, the Attorney-General.
The Court must allow the person protected by the order to be heard on the application if that person wishes.
The Court may grant leave under subsection (1) if the Court is satisfied there is evidence that—
the appeal has merit; and
is not an abuse of process.
If leave is granted under this section, the appropriate registrar for the Court must serve notice of the hearing date for the appeal on—
the vexatious litigant; and
the person protected by the order; and
if the Attorney-General made the application under section 189(1)(a) for the order declaring the person to be a vexatious litigant, the Attorney-General.

nodes.heading: Application for leave to appeal under Division 9 of Part 4 by vexatious litigant

nodes.text: A person who has been declared a vexatious litigant under this Part may appeal under Division 9 of Part 4 to the County Court or the Supreme Court against a decision referred to in section 114(2)(d) only if that Court grants leave for the appeal.

Section 114 provides for appeals in relation to family violence intervention orders.  For the right of a person to appeal against an order declaring the person to be a vexatious litigant see section 195.

If an application for leave to appeal is made to the County Court or the Supreme Court, the appropriate registrar for the court that made the order declaring the person to be a vexatious litigant must—
file in the County Court or the Supreme Court (as the case may be) a statement of the court's reasons for declaring the person to be a vexatious litigant; and
serve a copy of the statement and a copy of the application on—
the Attorney-General; and
the protected person in relation to the decision the subject of the appeal; and
if the protected person is not the person protected by the order declaring a person to be a vexatious litigant, the person protected by that order.

The protected person is entitled to be heard by the County Court or the Supreme Court on the application even if the protected person was not a party to the proceeding in which the order declaring the person to be a vexatious litigant was made.

In deciding whether to grant leave for an appeal under subsection (1), the County Court or Supreme Court must have regard to all the circumstances of the case, including the statement of reasons filed by the appropriate registrar for the court that made the order declaring the person to be a vexatious litigant.

nodes.heading: Court may vary, set aside or revoke

nodes.text: The court, as constituted under section 188, may at any time vary, set aside or revoke an order made under section 193 if it considers it proper to do so.
However, a vexatious litigant may apply to vary, set aside or revoke an order made under section 193 only with the leave of a magistrate of the court.
A magistrate may grant leave under subsection (2) if the magistrate is satisfied there is evidence that—
there is merit in the application; and
the application is not an abuse of the process of the court.
The appropriate registrar for the court must serve a copy of the application for leave on—
the person protected by the order declaring the person to be a vexatious litigant; and
if the Attorney-General made the application under section 189(1)(a) for the order declaring the person to be a vexatious litigant, the Attorney-General.
If leave is granted under subsection (2), the appropriate registrar for the court must serve notice of the hearing date for the application to vary, set aside or revoke the order on—
the person protected by the order; and
if the Attorney-General made the application under section 189(1)(a) for the order declaring the person to be a vexatious litigant, the Attorney-General.

nodes.heading: Attorney-General to publish copy of order in Government Gazette

nodes.text: The Attorney-General must cause a copy of any order made under section 193 or 197 to be published in the Government Gazette.
However, the copy of the order published in the Government Gazette must have removed from it the name of the person against whom the vexatious litigant must not make an application.

nodes.heading: Notice of order to be served on courts
nodes.text: If the court makes an order under section 193, a copy of the notice must be filed in—
the County Court and Supreme Court; and
if the order is made by the Magistrates' Court, the Children's Court; and
if the order is made by the Children's Court, the Magistrates' Court.

nodes.heading: Annual report
nodes.text: The Magistrates' Court and Children's Court must each give to the Attorney-General annually a report about the number of orders made under this Part declaring persons to be vexatious litigants. __________________

nodes.heading: Service of family violence intervention orders
nodes.text: If the court makes, varies, extends or revokes a family violence intervention order, the appropriate registrar for the court must—
arrange for the order to be drawn up and filed in the court; and
serve a copy of the order on the respondent; and
give a copy of the order to the following persons—
the Chief Commissioner of Police;
each party to the proceeding;
if the protected person is a child and the application was made with the consent of the child's parent, that parent;

if the protected person is a child and the order was made by the court relying on section 77(2), 103(b) or 104(a)(i), a parent of the child (other than the respondent) with whom the child normally or regularly lives;
if the protected person has a guardian, the guardian;
the officer in charge of the police station closest to the place of residence of the protected person.
This section applies if, under this Act, a document must be served on a person.
The document must be served on the person by giving a true copy of the document to the person personally.
Subject to subsection (4), if it appears to the court that it is not reasonably practicable to serve a copy of a document on a person personally, the court may—
order that a copy of the document be served by any other means it considers appropriate; or
make an order for substituted service.
An order under subsection (3) may not be made with respect to the service of a family violence safety notice.
As soon as practicable after a person serves a document under this Act, the person must file with the court a certificate of service—
that has been made on oath or by affidavit or is certified; and
that states service has taken place; and
that specifies details of the service.
For the purposes of subsection (1)(a), the certificate of service may certify that service has taken place only if that service was by a police officer or the appropriate registrar of a court.
The certificate of service must—
include the prescribed information; and
be accompanied by the prescribed documents.
A certificate of service is admissible in evidence and, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, is proof of the matters stated in it.

If a person is required under this Act to serve a document and it has not been possible to serve the document, the person must file with the court a certificate about why it has not been possible to serve the document.
The certificate must—
include the prescribed information; and
be accompanied by the prescribed documents.
A certificate under this section is admissible in evidence and, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, is proof of the matters stated in it.

nodes.heading: Person may cause document to be served

nodes.text: If, under this Act, a person is required or permitted to serve a document, the person may serve the document by causing it to be served by another person.
If, under this Act, a person is required or permitted to give a document to another person, the person may give the document by causing it to be given by another person.

nodes.heading: Certificate of service
nodes.text: If, under this Act, a police officer or appropriate registrar of a court is required or permitted to certify that a document has been served on a person, the police officer or appropriate registrar must complete a certificate of service that—
if the certificate is completed by a police officer, includes the police officer's name, rank and station; and
if the certificate is completed by an appropriate registrar, includes the appropriate registrar's name and the location of the court; and
includes a statement about the manner of service; and
includes a statement of the date, time and place of service; and
is certified by the police officer or appropriate registrar.
This section applies if—
a police officer applies to an organisation in the prescribed way for information held by the organisation about a respondent; and
the purpose of the application is to assist a police officer to locate the respondent to enable a police officer to serve the respondent with a document under this Act.
If the organisation has the information requested in the application, the organisation must give the police officer the information.
Information provided by an organisation under subsection (2) to a police officer—
must relate only to the respondent, or an associate of the respondent for whom an order has been made or is being sought under this Act; and
must not be used by a police officer for any purpose other than locating the respondent for the purpose of serving the respondent with a document under this Act; and
must not be given by a police officer to—
the protected person; or
any other organisation or person, other than another police officer or the court.
In this section—

nodes.text: It is the intention of sections 118 and 120 to alter or vary section 85 of the Constitution Act 1975.

nodes.heading: Rules of court and practice directions for Magistrates' Court

nodes.text: The Chief Magistrate together with 2 or more Deputy Chief Magistrates may jointly make rules of court for or with respect to proceedings in the Magistrates' Court in relation to applications and orders made under this Act.
Without limiting subsection (1), rules may be made for or with respect to the following matters—
the proper venue for proceedings under this Act, including the transfer of proceedings between court venues;
the right of parties to appear personally or to be represented by a legal practitioner;
the amendment of applications;
the striking out or dismissal by the court of matters;
the adjournment of proceedings by the court and the power to stay orders;
processes for filing family violence safety notices in the court;
access to records and documents held by the court;
extracts from records and documents held by the court and certification of those extracts.

A power conferred by this Act to make rules may be exercised in accordance with section 16(1D) and 16(1E) of the Magistrates' Court Act 1989 as if the rules had been made under section 16 of that Act.

To remove any doubt, it is declared that the power of the Chief Magistrate to issue practice directions, statements or notes for the court under section 16A of the Magistrates' Court Act 1989 in relation to civil proceedings or any class of civil proceedings includes power to issue practice directions, statements or notes for the court in relation to proceedings, or any class of proceedings, with respect to applications or orders made under this Act.

A practice direction, statement or note issued with respect to proceedings, or any class of proceedings, with respect to applications under this Act is taken to have been issued under section 16A(1) of the Magistrates' Court Act 1989.

nodes.heading: Rules of court and practice directions for Children's Court

nodes.text: The President of the Children's Court together with 2 or more magistrates of the court may jointly make rules for or with respect to proceedings in the court in relation to applications and orders made under this Act.
Without limiting subsection (1), rules may be made for or with respect to the following matters—
the proper venue for proceedings under this Act, including the transfer of proceedings between court venues;
the right of parties to appear personally or to be represented by a legal practitioner;
the amendment of applications;
the striking out or dismissal by the court of matters;
the adjournment of proceedings by the court and the power to stay orders;
processes for filing family violence safety notices in the court;
access to records and documents held by the court;
extracts from records and documents held by the court and certification of those extracts.
Rules made under subsection (1) may adopt or apply rules made for the Magistrates' Court under section 209.

To remove any doubt, it is declared that the power of the President of the Children's Court to issue practice directions, statements or notes for the court under section 592 of the Children, Youth and Families Act 2005 in relation to proceedings in the Family Division or the Criminal Division, or any class of proceedings in the Family Division or Criminal Division, includes power to issue practice directions, statements or notes for the court in relation to proceedings, or any class of proceedings, with respect to applications or orders made under this Act.

A practice direction, statement or note issued with respect to proceedings, or any class of proceedings, with respect to applications or orders under this Act is taken to have been issued under section 592(1) of the Children, Youth and Families Act 2005.
The Governor in Council may make regulations for or with respect to any matter or thing required or permitted by this Act to be prescribed or necessary to be prescribed to give effect to this Act.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may prescribe—
the content of forms to be used for the purposes of this Act; and
matters relevant to applications made under this Act; and
the content of orders, applications, notices and certificates made under this Act. __________________

nodes.heading: Repeal of Crimes (Family Violence) Act 1987 The Crimes (Family Violence) Act 1987 is repealed.
Definitions
nodes.text: In this Division—

nodes.heading: commencement day
nodes.text: means the day this section commences;

nodes.heading: interim intervention order
nodes.text: means an interim intervention order made under the repealed Act on grounds referred to in section 8 of that Act;

nodes.heading: intervention order
nodes.text: means—
an intervention order made under the repealed Act on grounds referred to in section 4 or 4A of that Act; or
an intervention order referred to in paragraph (a) that was subsequently varied or extended under section 16 or 16A of that Act;

nodes.heading: new Act
nodes.text: means the Family Violence Protection Act 2008;

nodes.heading: repealed Act
nodes.text: means the Crimes (Family Violence) Act 1987.

nodes.heading: References to repealed Act
nodes.text: On and from the commencement day, a reference in an Act (other than the new Act) or a document to the repealed Act is taken, if the context permits, to be a reference to the new Act.

On and from the commencement day, an intervention order made under the repealed Act (including an intervention order made in proceedings referred to in section 219) is taken to be a final order made under the new Act.
Without limiting subsection (1), the intervention order—
continues subject to any condition included in the order as if the condition had been included in the order under the new Act; and
the order may be revoked, varied or extended under the new Act as if it had been made under that Act.

nodes.heading: Interim intervention orders
nodes.text: On and from the commencement day, an interim intervention order made under the repealed Act (including an interim intervention order made in proceedings referred to in section 219) is taken to be an interim order made under the new Act.

nodes.heading: Counselling orders
nodes.text: On and from the commencement day, a counselling order made under the repealed Act (including a counselling order made in proceedings referred to in section 219) is taken to be a counselling order made under the new Act.

This section applies if, immediately before the commencement day, a complaint for an intervention order or an application for the variation, revocation or extension of an intervention order or an interim intervention order had been made under the repealed Act but a proceeding in relation to the complaint or application had not yet started.

On and from the commencement day, the complaint or application may be dealt with under the new Act as an application for a family violence intervention order or the variation, revocation or extension of an order as if it were an application made under that Act.

Section 7A(2) of the repealed Act continues to apply to a police officer in relation to a complaint or application made by that police officer under the repealed Act, or in relation to the police officer representing another police officer at a hearing in accordance with section 7A(1) of that Act, as if section 7A of the repealed Act had not been repealed.
This section applies if, immediately before the commencement day—
proceedings for an intervention order or interim intervention order, or the variation, revocation or extension of an order, had started but had not yet been finalised; or
an appeal under section 20 or 21 of the repealed Act had been started but had not yet been finalised; or
proceedings for an offence against section 22 of the repealed Act had started but had not yet been finalised.
The proceeding may continue under the repealed Act as if that Act had not been repealed.
This section applies if, immediately before the commencement day—
an interim intervention order had been made in relation to a complaint for an intervention order; but
proceedings for the final hearing of the complaint had not yet started.

The proceedings for the final hearing of the complaint may proceed under the new Act as if it were an application under that Act and the interim intervention order were an interim order made under that Act.

nodes.heading: Acts committed before commencement day relevant

nodes.text: This section applies if—
after the commencement day, a person (the first person) applies for a family violence intervention order against another person (the second person); and
before the commencement day, the first person and second person were not considered family members under the repealed Act.

Family violence committed before the commencement day may be taken into account by the court in deciding whether to make a family violence intervention order for the first person against the second person.

nodes.heading: Protection for protected person applies to acts committed before commencement day

nodes.text: This section applies if—

an aggrieved family member aided, abetted, counselled or procured the commission of an offence against the repealed Act because the aggrieved family member encouraged, permitted or authorised conduct by the defendant that breached an intervention order under the repealed Act; and

immediately before the commencement day the person had not been charged under section 52 of the Magistrates' Court Act 1989 with the offence or, if the person had been charged under that section, the charge had not been dealt with.
On and from the commencement day—
section 125 of the new Act applies to the person; and

the person cannot be charged with an offence under section 52 of the Magistrates' Court Act 1989 for the aiding, abetting, counselling or procuring or, if the person has already been charged, the charge must be withdrawn.

An interstate summary protection order registered in the court immediately before the commencement day is taken, on and from the commencement day, to be a corresponding interstate order registered under the new Act.

A New Zealand protection order registered in the court immediately before the commencement day is taken, on and from the commencement day, to be a corresponding New Zealand order registered under the new Act.
This section applies to an order made under a law of another State or a Territory and registered under section 18AA of the Crimes (Family Violence) Act 1987 before the commencement of this section.
An order referred to in subsection (1)—

is taken to be an interstate summary protection order within the meaning of section 3(1) of the Crimes (Family Violence) Act 1987, whether or not the State or Territory law under which the order was made had been declared by Order of the Governor in Council; and
to the extent that it is taken to be an interstate summary protection order, is taken to have been validly registered under section 18AA of the Crimes (Family Violence) Act 1987. __________________

In section 4L(1) of the Magistrates' Court Act 1989, for "an intervention order or interim intervention order" substitute "a family violence intervention order".

In section 4O(3)(e) of the Magistrates' Court Act 1989, for "Crimes (Family Violence) Act 1987" substitute "Family Violence Protection Act 2008".

nodes.heading: Amendments to the Residential Tenancies Act 1997
Definitions In section 3(1) of the Residential Tenancies Act
insert— "exclusion condition means an exclusion
nodes.text: condition included—
in a family violence safety notice under section 29 of the Family Violence Protection Act 2008; or

in a family violence intervention order under section 82 of that Act; family violence intervention order and family violence safety notice have the meanings given by the Family Violence Protection Act 2008;".

nodes.heading: Locks In section 70(5) of the Residential Tenancies Act
nodes.text: 1997, for "section 71" substitute "sections 70A and 71".

nodes.heading: New section 70A inserted After section 70 of the Residential Tenancies Act
insert— "70A Locks for rented premises the subject of a family violence intervention order

nodes.text: This section applies if—
a tenant is excluded from rented premises because of an exclusion condition included in a family violence intervention order or family violence safety notice; and
a protected person under the family violence intervention order or family violence safety notice—
is also a party to the tenancy agreement for the rented premises; or
has been residing in the rented premises as the protected person's principal place of residence but is not a party to the tenancy agreement.

The protected person may change any external door or window lock, including a lock in a master key system, of the rented premises, whether or not the protected person is a party to the tenancy agreement.
As soon as practicable after the protected person changes any external door or window lock, the protected person must—
give the landlord or landlord's agent—
a key to the lock; and
either a certified extract of the family violence intervention order or family violence safety notice or a copy of the order or notice; and
give a key to the lock to the parties to the tenancy agreement, other than the excluded tenant.
The protected person is not required to give the excluded tenant a key to the lock—
in the case of a family violence intervention order, unless the exclusion condition in the family violence intervention order ends; or
in the case of a family violence safety notice, until the family violence safety notice ends.

A landlord or landlord's agent must not give the excluded tenant any key provided under subsection (3)(a) if he or she knows that the tenant has been excluded from the rented premises under a family violence intervention order or family violence safety notice.

If a certified extract or a copy of a notice or order has been given to a landlord or landlord's agent under subsection (3)(a)(ii), the landlord and landlord's agent are taken to know that the tenant has been excluded from the rented premises.
A landlord or landlord's agent may only disclose, or give a copy of, a certified extract or a copy of a notice or order received under subsection (3)(a)(ii) to—
if given to the landlord, the landlord's agent;
if given to the landlord's agent, the landlord;
in either case, the legal representative of the landlord or landlord's agent;
any other person as prescribed.
This section applies despite anything in section 70.".

nodes.heading: Grounds for entry of rented premises

nodes.text: In section 86(1)(f) of the Residential Tenancies Act 1997, for "months." substitute "months; or".

After section 86(1)(f) of the Residential Tenancies Act 1997 insert— "(g) entry is required to enable inspection of the premises for the purposes of proceedings arising from or relating to an application made under section 233A(3).".

After section 86(3) of the Residential Tenancies Act 1997 insert— "(4) For the purposes of an inspection under subsection (1)(g), the excluded tenant may have a representative present at the inspection of the premises, but must provide the name and contact details of the representative to the landlord or landlord's agent before the inspection.".

nodes.heading: What must be in a notice of entry?

nodes.text: In section 88(c)(ii) of the Residential Tenancies Act 1997, for "6 p.m." substitute "6 p.m.; and".

After section 88(c)(ii) of the Residential Tenancies Act 1997 insert— "(d) if entry is pursuant to section 86(1)(g), and the landlord has been given the name and contact details required under that paragraph, state the name of the excluded tenant's representative (if any).".

nodes.heading: New sections 233A to 233D inserted
nodes.text: After section 233 of the Residential Tenancies Act 1997 insert— "233A Application for new tenancy agreement because of final family violence intervention order
In this section—

nodes.heading: final order
nodes.text: means a final order within the meaning of the Family Violence Protection Act 2008.
This section applies if—
a tenant is excluded from rented premises under an exclusion condition included in a final order; and
a protected person under the final order—
is also a party to the tenancy agreement for the rented premises; or
has been residing in the rented premises as the protected person's principal place of residence but is not a party to the tenancy agreement.
The protected person may apply to the Tribunal for an order—
terminating the existing tenancy agreement; and
requiring the landlord of the premises to enter into a tenancy agreement with the protected person and other persons (if any) specified in the application.
For the purposes of proceedings in relation to an application for an order under subsection
, each of the following persons is a party to the proceeding—
the protected person;
the landlord;
the excluded tenant;
any other existing tenants.

nodes.heading: Tribunal orders for application made under section 233A(3)

nodes.text: On receipt of an application under section 233A(3), the Tribunal may make an order terminating the existing tenancy agreement and requiring the landlord to enter into a new tenancy agreement with the protected person and other persons (if any) specified in the application if the Tribunal is satisfied that—
the protected person and other persons (if any) could reasonably be expected to comply with the duties of a tenant under a tenancy agreement to which this Act applies; and
the protected person or the protected person's dependent children would be likely to suffer severe hardship if the protected person were compelled to leave the premises; and
the hardship suffered by the protected person would be greater than any hardship the landlord would suffer if the order were made; and
it is reasonable to do so given the length of the exclusion under the final order and the length of the existing tenancy agreement; and

it is reasonable to do so given the interests of any other tenants (other than the excluded tenant) under the existing tenancy agreement and, in particular, whether the other tenants support the protected person's application.
If the Tribunal makes an order under subsection (1) the new tenancy agreement must—
be subject to the same rent and frequency of rent payments as the existing tenancy agreement; and
if the existing tenancy agreement is a fixed term agreement, run for a term not longer than the remainder of that fixed term; and
otherwise, be on the same terms and conditions as the existing tenancy agreement, subject to any changes the Tribunal determines.
If the Tribunal makes an order under subsection (1) the existing tenancy agreement is terminated on the signing of the new tenancy agreement.

nodes.heading: Tribunal may determine parties' liability under terminated tenancy agreement

nodes.text: If the Tribunal decides to make an order under section 233B, the Tribunal may determine the liabilities of the excluded tenant, the protected person or any other tenants under the existing tenancy agreement in relation to a bond paid for the rented premises and any other existing liabilities under the existing tenancy agreement, including, for example—
liabilities relating to damage caused to the rented premises; and
liabilities relating to outstanding utility charges.

To remove doubt, the termination of a tenancy agreement under section 233B does not give rise to a right to claim compensation on the part of any party to the agreement for early termination of the agreement.
For the purpose of making a determination under subsection (1), the Tribunal may adjourn the hearing to allow an inspection of the rented premises in accordance with section 86(1)(g).

nodes.heading: Cross-examination in proceedings for a new tenancy agreement

nodes.text: In a hearing for proceedings arising out of, or relating to, an application under section 233A(3) an excluded tenant must not personally cross-examine a protected person without leave of the Tribunal.
The Tribunal may grant leave under subsection (1) with or without conditions.
If leave is granted under subsection (1), the excluded tenant may only cross-examine the protected person—
as to those matters set out in section 233(1) and 233B(1); and
in accordance with any conditions to which the leave granted is subject.".

nodes.heading: Reduction of fixed term tenancy agreement
nodes.text: After section 234(2) of the Residential Tenancies Act 1997 insert— "(2A) Without limiting subsection (2), the Tribunal may be satisfied the applicant has experienced an unforeseen change in the applicant's circumstances that will cause the applicant to suffer severe hardship for the purposes of that subsection if—
the applicant is a tenant under the fixed term tenancy agreement; and
the applicant—
is excluded from the rented premises the subject of the agreement under a family violence intervention order; or
is a protected person under a family violence intervention order and is seeking to reduce the term of the agreement to protect their own safety or the safety of their children.".

nodes.heading: Service of documents
nodes.text: After section 506(3) of the Residential Tenancies Act 1997 insert— "(4) If, under this Act, a notice or other document is to be served or given to a person who is a tenant excluded from rented premises under a family violence safety notice or a family violence intervention order, the notice or document must be served or given—
by delivering it personally to the person; or

by leaving it at the address nominated by the person under section 33 or 85 of the Family Violence Protection Act 2008 with a person apparently over the age of 16 years and apparently residing or employed at that place; or
by sending it to the person by post or email to the address nominated by the person under section 33 or 85 of the Family Violence Protection Act 2008; or

by leaving it at the person's last known address (other than a place from which the person is excluded under the Family Violence Protection Act 2008) with a person apparently over the age of 16 years and apparently residing or employed at that place; or

by sending it to the person by post or email to the person's last known postal or email address (other than to an address from which the person is excluded under the Family Violence Protection Act 2008); or
in the manner ordered by the Tribunal.".

nodes.heading: Home detention
nodes.text: For section 18ZV(d) of the Sentencing Act 1991 substitute— "(d) a contravention of a family violence intervention order under the Family Violence Protection Act 2008, or an order of a corresponding nature made in another State or a Territory; or".

nodes.heading: Contents of home detention assessment report
nodes.text: For section 99G(1)(l) of the Sentencing Act 1991 substitute— "(l) an assessment of the likelihood that the offender will commit an offence in respect of which a family violence intervention order could be made under the Family Violence Protection Act 2008;".

nodes.heading: Amendments to the Victorian Civil and Administrative Tribunal Act 1998
New clause 62A of Schedule 1
nodes.text: After clause 62 of Schedule 1 to the Victorian Civil and Administrative Tribunal Act 1998 insert— "62A Support person

If a party to a proceeding under the Residential Tenancies Act 1997 is a protected person or a respondent under a family violence intervention order under the Family Violence Protection Act 2008, the party may be accompanied at a hearing by a person (a support person) for the purposes of that person providing support to the party.
The support person may be—
a legal practitioner; or
a social worker; or
a friend or family member of the party; or
any other person chosen by the party.".

nodes.heading: New clauses 73A and 73B of Schedule 1
nodes.text: After clause 73 of Schedule 1 to the Victorian Civil and Administrative Tribunal Act 1998 insert— "73A Evidence Despite section 102(1)(b), if any of the parties to a proceeding under the Residential Tenancies Act 1997 are the protected person and the respondent under the same family violence intervention order under the Family Violence Protection Act 2008, the respondent is not allowed to personally cross-examine the protected person unless the Tribunal gives the respondent leave to do so.
The Tribunal may direct that any of the following alternative arrangements be made for the giving of evidence by a witness in a proceeding under the Residential Tenancies Act 1997—

permitting the evidence to be given from a place other than the hearing room by means of closed circuit television or other facilities that enable communication between that place and the hearing room;
using screens to remove a party from the witness's direct line of vision;
permitting a person to be beside the witness while the witness is giving evidence for the purpose of providing emotional support to the witness;
requiring legal practitioners to be seated while examining or cross-examining the witness;
permitting only persons specified by the Tribunal to be present while the witness is giving evidence;
any other alternative arrangements the Tribunal considers appropriate.
If the witness is 18 years of age or over, the Tribunal may make a direction under subclause (1) on its own initiative or on the application of a party to the proceeding.
If the witness is under 18 years of age, the Tribunal must make a direction under subclause (1) unless it considers it is not appropriate to do so having regard to—
the wishes expressed by the witness; and
the age and maturity of the witness; and
any other matters that the Tribunal considers relevant.

The Tribunal may hear an application under subclause (2), or ascertain the matters in subclause (3), in camera and, except as otherwise directed by the Tribunal, persons who are not parties to the proceeding or their representatives are not permitted to be present while the hearing takes place or the matters are being ascertained.

Any place outside the hearing room where a witness is permitted to give evidence under this section is to be taken to be part of the hearing room while the witness is there for the purpose of giving evidence.
The Tribunal may at any time in the course of the proceeding vary or revoke a direction made under subclause (1) on its own initiative or on the application of a party to the proceeding.
In this section—

nodes.heading: hearing room
nodes.text: means the room in which the hearing for the proceeding is being conducted.".
